rv.q: The creative team has adroitly expanded the special effects and choreography to fill the Nederlander stage on Broadway, where "Disaster!" opened Tuesday night.
Seth Rudetsky and Jack Plotnick's ingenious, blissfully silly jukebox musical
This shameless pastiche of 1970s disaster movies is performed with such gleeful commitment that you may find yourself grinning against your better judgment.

It is the caliber of these parodists that keeps the silliness afloat as Tony's earthquake-racked gambling vessel takes on ever more water. Butler, a star of Broadway's tongue-in-cheek "Hairspray" and "Xanadu," and Pascal, the original Roger in "Rent," approach their stock roles with a winning élan.....
But ultimately, 70s disaster movies were far more ludicrous than anything on this stage.

And yet, given the flock of genuine experts who signed on for the spree, it does seem fair to expect more than this sporadically clever, sweetly produced, fantastically performed spoof of a passe genre — the ’70s disaster movie — in overdone jukebox musical style.

Even appreciating the gratification of nostalgia and camp, Disaster! is an odd property to find on Broadway and doesn’t seem particularly at home here, with its cheap sets, shabby projections and understaffed chorus.

Roger Bart and Kerry Butler are featured in the musical “Disaster!” at the Nederlander Theatre in New York. In the great disaster-movie epics of the 1970s, star casting was a crucial weapon. Look darling, that's Jennifer Jones falling to her death in "The Towering Inferno"!
Though why anyone thought it was a good idea to move it to primetime Broadway remains a mystery.
Disaster! is a jukebox musical that uses '70s hits to soundtrack a spoof of '70s disaster movies, and it's about as clever as that sounds.
This creation of Sirius radio host Seth Rudetsky is the Broadway season's happiest surprise.
Disaster! is pure maximalism — a big, old-fashioned musical with big numbers and big performances.

It takes guts to call a Broadway show "Disaster!" That's just asking for audiences to say that it lives up to its name. But this spoof of catastrophe-themed movies set on a floating casino and mixed with '70s pop hits is not a Titanic -- or a jackpot. The campy entertainment lands halfway between. In other words, it's not "Hot Stuff"...
Even so, the show’s relentless, one-note silliness grows tiresome, resembling a “Saturday Night Live” sketch that goes on way too long.
By the time “Disaster” was over, I had laughed some, but mostly I was rooting for the piranhas.
For everyone else, though, this "disaster" of a musical might well leave you with a sinking feeling.
'Disaster' is too dynamic a word to describe the new jukebox musical 'Disaster!,'
Disaster! is exactly the kind of show that gives jukebox musicals a bad name

Disaster! is the Nick The Lounge Singer of Broadway musicals. A cast of extraordinarily gifted stars appears to have been tricked into stretching a three-minute parody of movies that were parodies to begin with into a two-hour show. The result is so painfully witless it's hard to tell where the sea-spray ends and the flop sweat begins.

And then there are the newcomers– Baylee Littrell (the literal Backstreet Boy), Jennifer Simard (who pretty much steals the show as a gambling addicted nun), and the stunning Lacretta Nicole (she could sing the whole show and I wouldn’t have minded). The 30 plus songs are not throwaways.
